explanation: In modern C++, algorithms like 'uninitialized_copy_n' are used to construct objects directly into uninitialized memory, typically allocated via allocators or raw memory buffers. This approach is essential for custom memory management, container implementation, and performance-critical applications, as it allows precise control over object lifetime and construction without default-initializing memory. These algorithms utilize placement new internally to construct objects in-place, ensuring exception safety and optimal resource management.
keywords: Placement new, Uninitialized algorithms, In-place construction, Raw memory construction
